summary: The Manual Q&A on Tough and Balanced gives opposite orders for a Tough mod on a Balanced unit. Its first sentence says Tough "augmented onto" a Balanced unit is doubled, then balanced; its last sentence says Tough "applied to" a Balanced unit is balanced, then doubled. The owner ruling of 2026-08-18 (“Stat layer 4 application order”) says the order between printed, mod-given and column-shared attributes is the engine's own call, and the engine balances first.

resolution: Answered by the owner on 2026-10-22 (CT-257): reading A, the Manual p.42 first clause. Tough augmented onto a Balanced unit is doubled, then balanced; the last clause ("applied to") is a grant by an effect, which balances, then doubles. effects.continuous.layers.attribute-order and attr.general.application-order state it alone. Engine fix: done 2026-10-22 (F-U16-4, F-U19-5 closed): 08-cards2 drives both clauses.

summary: The Manual lists Inverted as its own layer after the attribute layer, and the owner ruling of 2026-08-28 (“{Tough} + {Inverted}: the owner's own…”) makes the result independent of grant order. Caleb, quoted in the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”), said "Tough inverted balanced would be different" from Tough balanced inverted, which reads as Inverted taking a place inside layer 4.

resolution: Not a question: the two readings differ only for a unit that gains Tough, then Inverted, then Balanced, and Caleb himself says that order is "basically impossible to make happen", because Tough and Inverted together kill the unit first (the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”); the owner ruling of 2026-08-28 (“{Tough} + {Inverted}: the owner's own…”): they leave defense 0). The rules follow the Manual's layer list (Inverted after all of layer 4), which every reachable board agrees with. Caleb's "Tough inverted balanced would be different" is recorded; if a card ever grants the three in that order at once, his interleaved reading applies, and the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 (“Stat layer 5: {Inverted} negates the…”) names the engine change.

summary: The owner ruling of 2026-10-10 (“A copy's copied augments work: it…”) says text a copy inherits is as old as the copy's printed text, so any strip takes it. The RAQ says an attribute or ability a unit gains after a strip is not taken. The two part only for a copy that begins on a unit already stripped.

sides.quote: so it is exactly as old as the copy's printed text (R328)

resolution: Not a question today. The owner ruling of 2026-10-10 (“A copy's copied augments work: it…”) and the RAQ agree for Borrower of Forms, which enters play already a copy. They part only for an until-regroup copy (Apex Prime) made on a unit already stripped by Suppression Field or Formless: the RAQ's "later gains" (designer authority) would let the copied text survive the earlier strip if becoming a copy is gaining abilities, and the owner ruling of 2026-10-10 (“A copy's copied augments work: it…”) says it is not. The rule states the owner ruling of 2026-10-10 (“A copy's copied augments work: it…”). A question for the owner only if that board arises.

summary: Whether a unit stripped by a continuous effect (Transmogrifant, Monke) stops applying its own static abilities. Printed text strips all abilities and the owner ruling of 2026-08-21 (“The suppression layer: "loses all attributes…”) says a static is an ability; the owner ruling of 2026-08-21 (“The suppression layer: "loses all attributes…”) and the owner ruling of 2026-10-09 (“Stripping is a layer applied in…”) encode static-vs-static in one pass that reads only the one-time stamp, so such a unit keeps applying its statics. The owner ruling of 2026-08-21 (“The suppression layer: "loses all attributes…”) justifies the one pass only by the mutual case.

resolution: Settled by printed text and the owner (2026-10-16: "Everything (besides an attribute) is an ability."): Transmogrifant's "lose all attributes and abilities" takes every ability, statics included, and effects.stripping.what.abilities states it. summary: The sources are silent on whether deaths are checked part-way through an effect's resolution. The owner ruling of 2026-10-06 (“No action ends with a dead…”) makes the end of every action a safe point and says a suspended action is not at one; it does not say whether the effect's own changes are checked as they happen. The engine checks after each counter placement and after each part of a composite effect, so units an 'each unit' effect kills (Pestilent Titan) die one at a time, not together.
